findings.title: Smooth on a list of datasets smooths ACROSS dataset boundaries, silently mixing subjects' data
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
a = np.zeros((30, 2)); b = np.ones((30, 2))
sm = hyp.manip([a, b], model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, maintain_bounds=False)
print(np.asarray(sm[0], dtype=float)[-3:, 0])  # expected [0. 0. 0.]
print(np.asarray(sm[1], dtype=float)[:3, 0])   # expected [1. 1. 1.]
findings.expected: Each dataset smoothed independently: sm[0] stays all zeros, sm[1] stays all ones (a constant signal is invariant under smoothing).
findings.actual:
ds0 unchanged (all 0): False  ds0 tail: [0.03962704 0.2004662  0.3962704 ]
ds1 unchanged (all 1): False  ds1 head: [0.6037296  0.7995338  0.96037296]
gaussian ds0 all 0: False ds1 all 1: False

findings.title: Resample axis=1 crashes with DTypePromotionError on any DataFrame with string column names
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3), columns=list('abc'))
hyp.manip(df, model='Resample', axis=1, n_samples=9)
findings.expected: Either resample each row over column positions (documented behavior), or a clear error explaining that axis=1 requires numeric column labels.
findings.actual: DTypePromotionError: The DType <class 'numpy.dtypes._PyFloatDType'> could not be promoted by <class 'numpy.dtypes.StrDType'>. This means that no common DType exists for the given inputs. For example they cannot be stored in a single array un...

findings.title: Fitted Smooth cannot be reused on data with different column labels: bare KeyError (ZScore/Normalize got the positional-keying fix, Smooth did not)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.randn(40, 3)
_, ms = hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, return_model=True)
newdf = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(40, 3), columns=['roi1', 'roi2', 'roi3'])
hyp.manip(newdf, model=ms)
findings.expected: Smoothed (40,3) output, matching ZScore's behavior in the identical scenario ('ZScore fit-on-array->reuse-on-nameddf: OK (40, 3)').
findings.actual:
KeyError: 'roi1'   (with 3 differently-named cols)
KeyError: 'w'      (with 4 cols; no count guard)

findings.title: Fitted Smooth reuse replays FIT-TIME min/max bounds onto new data, silently clipping it to the old range
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
df = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(40, 3)), columns=list('abc'))
_, ms = hyp.manip(df, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, return_model=True)
new = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(loc=100.0, size=(30, 3)), columns=list('abc'))
out = hyp.manip(new, model=ms)
print(np.asarray(out, dtype=float).min(), np.asarray(out, dtype=float).max())
findings.expected: Smoothed values near 100 (clipping, if any, relative to the transformed data's own pre-smoothing range).
findings.actual: out range=[1.05,2.24] on input centered at 100 -- every output value equals its column's fit-time maximum.

findings.title: pandas Series input to manip() is wrangled to an EMPTY (0,0) DataFrame, then fails with nonsense errors
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
s = pd.Series(np.sin(np.linspace(0, 6, 40)), name='sig')
hyp.manip(s, model='ZScore')
findings.expected: Treat the Series as a (40,1) dataset (as hyp.normalize does), or raise a clear 'unsupported type' error naming Series and the fix.
findings.actual:
dw.wrangle(Series) -> DataFrame (0, 0)
manip(Series, ZScore) -> IndexError: list index out of range
manip(Series, Smooth) -> ValueError: kernel_width (11) is larger than the number of samples (0); use a kernel_width <= 0.

findings.title: manip ZScore returns all-NaN for single-row (and 1-D) input; hyp.normalize returns zeros for the same input
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.manip(np.array([1., 2., 3., 4.]), model='ZScore'))
print(hyp.normalize(np.array([1., 2., 3., 4.])))
findings.expected: Either zeros (matching hyp.normalize/sklearn convention) or a clear error; not silent NaN. 1-D orientation consistent between the two APIs.
findings.actual:
E5.manip-1d -> (1, 4) [nan nan nan nan]
E5.normalize-1d -> (4, 1) [-1.34164079 -0.4472136   0.4472136   1.34164079]
E3.manip-zscore-single-row values=[[nan nan nan]]

findings.title: manip() empty/None input errors are cryptic; empty LIST takes the text path and loads a topic-model corpus
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(), model='ZScore')   # IndexError
# hyp.manip([], model='ZScore')             # corpus load + LDA ValueError
# hyp.manip(None, model='ZScore')           # IndexError
findings.expected: A clear 'input has no observations' / 'unsupported input' error like hyp.normalize's, without loading text corpora.
findings.actual:
IndexError: list index out of range
loading corpus: minipedia...done! ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.

findings.title: Smooth's non-integer kernel_width warning says 'Rounding ... to the nearest integer' but the code truncates
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
from scipy.signal import savgol_filter
long = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.arange(50.)})
r = hyp.manip(long, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11.7, maintain_bounds=False)
print(np.allclose(np.asarray(r['y'], dtype=float), savgol_filter(np.arange(50.), 11, 3)))  # True -> truncated
findings.expected: Behavior matches the warning: 11.7 -> 12 -> (odd bump) 13; or the warning says 'Truncating'.
findings.actual: warnings: ['Rounding smoothing kernel width to the nearest integer']; effective width used: 11

findings.title: Documented ValueError cases actually raise AssertionError (stripped under python -O), and normalize's message names a nonexistent 'scale_type' parameter
findings.expected: ValueError (as documented), raised unconditionally, with the message naming the actual parameter ('normalize').
findings.actual:
AssertionError minimum must be strictly less than maximum
AssertionError scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: Dict spec with an unknown model name leaks 'AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'fit_transform''
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3)), model={'model': 'Bar', 'kwargs': {}})
findings.expected: The same clear ValueError as the bare-string path: "unknown manip model 'Bar'; supported names: Normalize, ZScore, Smooth, Resample ..."

findings.title: Invalid legacy mode= value is silently accepted (falls back to savgol); kernel= validates but mode= does not
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
r = hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3)), model='Smooth', mode='hann')
print(type(r))  # DataFrame -- no error, silently savgol
findings.expected: ValueError (or at least a warning) for mode values outside {'savgol', 'gaussian'}.

findings.title: Row-wise (axis=1) fitted ZScore/Normalize silently transform NEW data using fit-time per-row statistics
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3), columns=list('abc'))
_, m = hyp.manip(df, model='Normalize', axis=1, return_model=True)
out = hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 5)), model=m)
print(out.shape)  # (30, 5), silently used fit-time per-row baseline/peak
findings.expected: Error or per-row re-derivation; not silent reuse of fit-time row statistics on unrelated rows.

findings.title: manip is described as 'per-dataset' but ZScore/Normalize/Smooth fit ONE shared set of statistics across a list of datasets
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
z = hyp.manip([np.zeros((30, 2)), np.ones((30, 2))], model='ZScore')
print(np.asarray(z[0], dtype=float)[:2, 0])
findings.expected: Docs matching behavior: per-dataset wording implies each dataset z-scored by its own stats (0s here).
findings.actual: ZScore list: ds0 values (shared stats -> approx -1): [-0.99163165 -0.99163165]

findings.title: normalize() docstring says 'If the input was a list, a list is returned' -- false for single-element lists
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(type(hyp.normalize([np.random.randn(10, 3)])))
findings.expected: list (per docstring), or a docstring documenting the single-element unwrap.

findings.title: hyp.manip('ZScore') and hyp.normalize() z-score with DIFFERENT std conventions (ddof=1 vs ddof=0) -- same data, different numbers
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
H = np.array([[1., 0.], [2., 10.], [3., 20.], [4., 30.]])
print(np.asarray(hyp.manip(H, model='ZScore'), dtype=float).std(0, ddof=0))  # [0.866 0.866]
print(hyp.normalize(H, normalize='within').std(0, ddof=0))                   # [1. 1.]
findings.expected: One documented convention (or an explicit ddof parameter); docstrings stating which std is used.
findings.actual: manip ZScore axis=0: popstd=[0.8660254 0.8660254], sampstd=[1. 1.]; consistency manip-ZScore vs normalize-within: allclose = False

findings.title: Cross-API inconsistencies between manip() and normalize(): return types, DataFrame metadata, NaN handling, 1-D orientation
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(10, 3), columns=list('abc'))
print(type(hyp.manip(df, model='ZScore')))   # DataFrame, metadata kept
print(type(hyp.normalize(df)))               # ndarray, metadata lost
findings.expected: Consistent (or explicitly documented) conventions across the two functions.
findings.actual: manip -> DataFrame (index/columns preserved, NaN propagated); normalize -> ndarray (metadata lost, NaN imputed)

findings.title: The 'unknown manip model' error recommends the DEPRECATED dict form
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(5, 2)), model='Foo')
findings.expected: Error text recommending the canonical dict form.
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown manip model 'Foo'; supported names: Normalize, ZScore, Smooth, Resample (or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, a Manipulator subclass, or a Manipulator instance directly)

findings.title: Several common data problems surface as raw scipy/numpy internals with no hypertools context
findings.repro:

hyp.manip(dup, model='Resample', n_samples=8)
